# create_will XDR Spec Fixture
#
# This file contains the hex-encoded XDR of the `create_will` function's
# contract spec entry, as generated by the `#[contractimpl]` macro.
#
# PURPOSE
# -------
# The XDR spec fixture test (`test_xdr_spec.rs`) reads this file and
# compares it against the spec generated at test time from the
# `WillContract` implementation. If they differ, it means the `create_will`
# API has changed (parameter names, types, or order) without the fixture
# being updated — which is exactly the schema-drift signal we want to catch.
#
# HOW TO UPDATE
# -------------
# When you intentionally change the `create_will` signature (new parameter,
# type change, rename), update this fixture by running:
#
#   cargo test -p will --lib test_spec_fixture_create_will_update -- --nocapture
#
# That test prints the new hex to stdout and writes it here automatically.
# Commit both the code change and the updated fixture in the same PR so
# reviewers can see exactly what changed in the encoded spec.
#
# SDK COORDINATION
# ----------------
# The sorowill-sdk repo has a companion spec-drift-check (see sorowill-sdk
# issue #101). When this fixture changes, update the SDK's expected spec
# fixture in the same PR or open a coordinated follow-up PR there. Reference
# that PR in the description here so reviewers can verify both sides match.
#
# FIXTURE (hex, no whitespace)
